answer:
The most effective treatment for allergic rhinitis, according to the American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology guidelines from 2020, is an intranasal corticosteroid. This should be used as first-line therapy for moderate to severe or persistent symptoms; for mild and intermittent symptoms, a second-generation oral antihistamine can be used instead. It's also important to incorporate allergen avoidance as part of the management plan alongside medication use. 

[citation] [AAAAI/ACAAI Joint Practice Parameter, 2020][^1]

For more detailed information, you may refer to this guideline: 
[https://www.aaaai.org/allergist-resources/ask-the-expert/answers/2020/allergic-rhinitis]^2

[^1]: [AAAAI/ACAAI Joint Practice Parameter](https://www.aaaai.org/allergist-resources/ask-the-expert/answers/2020/allergic-rhinitis)
[^2]: [American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology](https://www.aaaai.org/)

results.content: For allergic rhinitis, an intranasal corticosteroid is the most effective single therapy and is recommended first-line for moderate to severe or persistent symptoms; a second-generation oral antihistamine is an alternative for mild, intermittent symptoms. Allergen avoidance is an adjunct to, not a substitute for, medication.
